paper_metadata.title: Benchmarking Highly Precise Quantum Linear Systems Algorithms

summary: The paper benchmarks the HHL quantum linear systems algorithm combined with classical iterative refinement on Quantinuum platforms. Hardware experiments solve 4×4 systems on the Quantinuum H2‑2 QPU, while emulator experiments handle up to 8 variables; for an 8‑variable system on the H1‑1LE emulator, iterative refinement reduces solution error from about 0.8488 to about 0.0008 (>10^3 improvement). The work demonstrates accuracy gains from hybrid refinement but does not measure runtime advantage over classical solvers.

experiments.description: HHL with iterative refinement (HHL-IR) benchmarked on Quantinuum hardware and emulators/simulators for solving small linear systems up to 8 variables.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative refinement loop continues until residual norm satisfies the target tolerance ζ
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical initialization with x(0)=0, r(0)=b̃, η(0)=1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: HHL solves a Hermitian linear system Ax=b using QPE-based eigenvalue estimation; the paper does not specify a qubit-by-qubit variable encoding beyond the HHL circuit structure
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve Ax=b and output a classical solution x satisfying ||Ax-b||/||b|| ≤ ζ
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative refinement uses residual correction Mu(k)=r(k) solved by the quantum linear solver at each step

problem_instance.description: Linear systems up to 4 variables executed on Quantinuum H2-2 hardware; systems up to 8 variables executed on Quantinuum emulators (H1-1LE and H1-1E noisy emulator).

dataset_specification.description: Problem instances are linear systems; one explicitly mentioned as an unstructured 4-variable system

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Systems are normalized using α̃=max{||A||F,||b||}; b̃=b/α̃ and Ã=A/α̃
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmarking across backends; compares HHL with and without iterative refinement; reports residuals and solution errors across problem sizes and QPE qubit counts

hardware.device_name: Quantinuum H2-2 (hardware); additional benchmarks on H1-1LE emulator and H1-1E noisy emulator
hardware.framework: Qiskit with pytket via Quantinuum qnexus

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on real QPU and noisy emulator/simulator backends

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: System normalization and residual computation for iterative refinement
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical update x(k+1)=x(k)+η(k)^{-1}ũ(k) and residual recomputation

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Residual and error decrease across iterative refinement iterations

speedup_claims.baseline_method: direct high-precision HHL / QLSA without iterative refinement
speedup_claims.conditions: when iterative refinement is used to improve low-precision quantum solutions; claimed in the context of reducing quantum resources and improving solution accuracy
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a claim about accuracy improvement and resource reduction, not a full end-to-end runtime speedup proof.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: HHL-based QLSA with QPE; paper states iterative refinement reduces quantum resources and can exponentially improve solution accuracy, but does not give a full asymptotic complexity expression

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiments limited to ≤4-variable systems on hardware and ≤8 variables on emulators with unspecified qubit counts.
limiting_factors: Very small problem sizes (≤4 variables on hardware).
No comparison with classical linear solvers in runtime or accuracy scaling.
Quantum phase estimation depth grows rapidly with precision.
Noise accumulation limits benefits of larger QPE registers on current hardware.
State preparation and matrix oracle costs not included in resource analysis.

notes: Hardware type is reported as Quantinuum H2-2; the provider/device imply a real trapped-ion QPU.
The paper reports problem sizes and QPE qubit-count variation but does not state a total qubit count or circuit depth explicitly, so these are null/inferred not reported.
Speedup order is taken from the paper's claim that iterative refinement can exponentially improve solution accuracy; this is not an asymptotic end-to-end runtime proof.
The authors discuss theoretical exponential advantages of QLSAs and accuracy improvements from iterative refinement but do not demonstrate runtime advantage over classical solvers.
Experiments are benchmarking and accuracy-improvement demonstrations on very small systems rather than advantage tests.

experiments.description: Benchmark of HHL with iterative refinement on the Quantinuum H1-1LE emulator for linear systems up to 8 variables.
key_results: For an 8-variable system, iterative refinement reduced solution error from approximately 0.8488 to approximately 0.0008 (>10^3 improvement).

experiments.description: Noisy emulator study (Quantinuum H1-1E) evaluating the effect of QPE register size and iterative refinement on residual error for 4-variable and 8-variable linear systems.
key_results: Residual error compared across different QPE qubit counts; deeper circuits with more QPE qubits degrade performance on noisy emulators, while iterative refinement consistently improves accuracy.
